zipCodeComparison.areaName: Northern & Western Clifton (Upper Montclair Heights, Richfield, Athenia, Albion)
zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Montclair Heights, Richfield, Athenia, Albion Place, Styertowne, Maple Valley
keyFindings: Generates ~43.6% of Clifton's residential property tax levy due to high-value colonials and larger lots in Montclair Heights and Richfield.
Significantly older median age (46.2 yrs) with high concentrations of long-tenured homeowners and empty-nesters.
Sends 3,400 students to district schools while contributing $70.6M in school taxes, producing a net educational fiscal surplus.
High homeownership rate (76.5%) means households directly bear quarterly property tax assessments via escrow.

zipCodeComparison.areaName: Central Clifton & Allwood Station (Suburban Enclave & Commercial Corridor)
zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Allwood, Allwood Road, Market Street Corridor, School #11 Zone
keyFindings: Highest homeownership rate in Clifton (81.4%) centered around the historic planned community of Allwood.
High assessment density generates $7.02 per square foot in taxes, among the highest effective spatial tax burdens in Passaic County.
Sends 980 students to School #11 and secondary schools while contributing $22.3M to school levy, acting as a net donor postal zone.
Bordered by Nutley and Bloomfield with commuter rail and express bus access via Allwood Road.

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Botany Village, Lakeview, Main Avenue Corridor, Dutch Hill, Historic Mill District
keyFindings: Highest relative tax-to-income economic burden in Clifton (15.01% of household paycheck) despite lower gross home valuations.
Enrolls 53.2% of all Clifton public school students (5,720 students), driven by younger median age (37.2 yrs) and dense multi-family housing.
Majority-renter population (52.2%) where property taxes are passed directly into monthly apartment rent ($350-$480/month embedded).
Balanced fiscally through $108.4M in State Equalization Aid which bridges the per-pupil funding requirement.

zipCodeComparison.areaName: Southern Clifton & Delawanna (Commuter Transit Corridor & Passaic River)
zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Delawanna, Kingsland Road, River Road, Route 3 Corridor, School #1 Zone
keyFindings: Balanced fiscal ratio: Delawanna pays 5.9% of the school tax levy and consumes 6.1% of district classroom seats.
Transit-oriented residential corridor adjacent to Delawanna train station and Route 3 express bus routes into Manhattan.
Mix of single-family post-war capes, townhouses, and commuter multi-family dwellings along the Passaic River.
Directly feeds School #1 (Delawanna) and Woodrow Wilson Middle School.

neighborhoods.name: Montclair Heights
neighborhoods.description: Hilly wooded neighborhood bordering Montclair and Upper Montclair. Characterized by large single-family colonial homes, expansive yards, and low housing turnover.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Pays the highest average property tax check in Clifton (~$18k/year). Demographics skew older with established professionals and many retirees.

neighborhoods.name: Allwood & Richfield
neighborhoods.description: Historic suburban neighborhoods centered around Allwood Road, Styertowne Shopping Center, and Route 3. Stable middle-to-upper-middle-class enclave.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: High proportion of long-time senior homeowners on fixed incomes who feel intense pressure when annual school budgets and county tax levies rise.

neighborhoods.name: Athenia
neighborhoods.description: Centrally located around Clifton Avenue and Athenia Steel Park. Walkable neighborhood with a balance of single-family homes, duplexes, and local bakeries.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Represents Clifton's statistical midpoint. Even balance of school-age families and senior residents paying ~$12,000 annually in taxes.

neighborhoods.name: Delawanna & Transit Corridor
neighborhoods.description: Located at Clifton's southern border near Nutley, Passaic River, and Route 3. Features the Delawanna NJ Transit train station, townhouse complexes, and heavy commercial retail.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Higher proportion of transit commuters and young working professionals. Heavy commercial ratables help offset residential municipal costs.

neighborhoods.name: Botany Village & Historic District
neighborhoods.character: Historic Industrial Textile Mill & High Density
neighborhoods.description: Historic neighborhood built around the former Botany Worsted Mills. Urban-suburban fabric with multi-family homes, pedestrian commercial streets, and vibrant Latino and Middle Eastern cultural commerce.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Highest tax-to-income burden (13.82%). Over 58% of households rent. Major contributor to elementary and middle school enrollment.

neighborhoods.name: Lakeview & Dutch Hill
neighborhoods.description: Northern Clifton bordering Paterson. Features a diverse mix of 2-family homes, bungalows, and multi-family properties with high family density.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Younger population with high child-to-adult ratio. Generates significant public school enrollment while facing high effective tax burdens relative to household earnings.

keyTakeaways.title: The 56.7% Income Gap Between ZIP Codes
keyTakeaways.detail: Median household income in 07013 ($116,273) is $42,079 higher than in 07011 ($74,194). This creates a stark division in economic resilience to property tax increases.

keyTakeaways.title: The Inverted Tax Burden (Tax Effort vs. Ability to Pay)
keyTakeaways.detail: Although 07013 pays higher nominal tax bills ($14.2k vs $10.0k), residents in 07011 pay a higher portion of their paycheck on property taxes (13.55% of household income vs. 12.24% in 07013).

keyTakeaways.title: The Inter-Neighborhood School Subsidy
keyTakeaways.detail: 07013 generates ~63% of Clifton's residential tax levy while supplying ~47% of students. 07011 supplies ~53% of public school students while contributing ~37% of the residential tax levy.

keyTakeaways.title: The Hidden Renter Burden
keyTakeaways.detail: 52% of 07011 households are renters. Because multi-family landlords pass 100% of property taxes into leases, working-class tenants pay an estimated $300 to $450 of their monthly rent directly toward municipal and school taxes.

zipBreakdown.area: East Clifton (Botany Village, Lakeview, Dutch Hill)
zipBreakdown.keyDriver: High density of 2-4 family homes, multi-generational households, and lower median age (37.2 yrs).

zipBreakdown.area: Allwood Station & Central Clifton (Allwood Road / Market St)
zipBreakdown.keyDriver: High homeownership (81.4%), planned suburban lots, School #11 zone, and $15.4k average tax bill.

zipBreakdown.area: Upper & Western Clifton (Montclair Heights, Richfield, Athenia, Albion)
zipBreakdown.keyDriver: Predominance of single-family colonials, older median age (46.2 yrs), high median incomes ($124k+).

zipBreakdown.area: Delawanna & South Clifton (Commuter Corridor & Passaic River)
zipBreakdown.keyDriver: Mix of townhomes, post-war singles, commuter proximity to Route 3, and School #1 zone.

schools.name: School #1 (Delawanna)
schools.notes: Serves Clifton's southern commuter corridor near Nutley border.

schools.name: School #2 (Athenia)
schools.notes: Centrally located school serving Athenia and surrounding residential blocks.

schools.name: School #3 (Paulison / Albion)
schools.notes: Serves western residential neighborhoods along Paulison Avenue.

schools.name: School #4 (Albion Place)
schools.notes: One of Clifton's smallest neighborhood elementary schools, nestled in a quiet hillside residential zone.

schools.name: School #5 (Valley Road)
schools.notes: Serves Upper Clifton and Valley Road area; lowest proportion of economically disadvantaged students in district.

schools.name: School #8 (Main Ave / Dutch Hill)
schools.notes: Serves northern Main Avenue corridor with dense commercial and multi-family ratables.

schools.name: School #9 (Lakeview)
schools.notes: Bordering Paterson; high density of young families and ESL / bilingual education support.

schools.name: School #11 (Allwood)
schools.notes: Serves the Allwood residential community; high homeowner tax contribution zone.

schools.name: School #12 (Dutch Hill / Clifton Ave)
schools.notes: Largest elementary school in Clifton; high child-per-household density.

schools.name: School #13 (Athenia / Van Houten)
schools.notes: Serves central Clifton along the Van Houten Avenue thoroughfare.

schools.name: School #14 (Botany Village / Lake Ave)
schools.notes: Located in the historic Botany Mill district; highest proportion of multilingual learners.

schools.name: School #15 (Botany Village / Highland)
schools.notes: Serves east Botany Village near Dundee Canal; high density of large multi-family households.

schools.name: School #16 (Montclair Heights)
schools.notes: Serves Clifton's highest assessed residential tax base; lowest density of school-age children per household.

schools.name: School #17 (Richfield)
schools.notes: Serves south-central Clifton; high concentration of single-family suburban homes.

schools.name: Woodrow Wilson Middle School
schools.notes: Consolidated middle school receiving elementary graduates from Schools 1, 8, 9, 12, 14, and 15.

schools.name: Christopher Columbus Middle School
schools.notes: Consolidated middle school receiving elementary graduates from Schools 2, 3, 4, 5, 11, 13, 16, and 17.

schools.name: Clifton High School (CHS)
schools.notes: Single consolidated comprehensive high school serving the entire City of Clifton; one of the largest high schools in New Jersey.
